published_statement: FLAG 2024 Sec.10.4.4 (as transcribed by the sibling audit's at-source read and by massform.py:1314-1350): Eq.(447) 'N_f = 2 + 1 + 1 : sigma_piN = 60.9(6.5) MeV Refs. [26, 101]'; Eq.(448) 'N_f = 2 + 1 : sigma_piN = 42.2(2.4) MeV Refs. [102-106]'; Eq.(449) 'N_f = 2 + 1 + 1 : sigma_s = 41.0(8.8) MeV Ref. [107]'; Eq.(450) 'N_f = 2 + 1 : sigma_s = 44.9(6.4) MeV Refs. [102-108]'. p.273: 'Notably, there is now a 2.7 sigma difference between the N_f = 2 + 1 and N_f = 2 + 1 + 1 FLAG averages. This is unlikely to be due to the inclusion of charm quarks in the sea. The control of excited-state contributions remains an issue. In particular, the PNDME 21 study utilizes a narrow-width prior ... If this constraint is relaxed then a sigma term of around 42 MeV is obtained.' p.274: 'The N_f = 2 + 1 + 1 lattice average is in agreement with Hoferichter et al. [1035] (Hoferichter 23 in Fig. 46), while there is some tension, at the level of around three standard deviations, with the lattice average for N_f = 2 + 1.' p.261: 'The sigma_piN,s,c give the shift in M_N due to nonzero light-, strange- and charm-quark masses.' Definition (Eqs.(431)-(433),(446)): sigma_q = m_q <N|qbar q|N> = m_q dM_N/dm_q (Feynman-Hellmann). p.275: ETM 19 sigma_c = 107(22) MeV (N_f = 2+1+1), RQCD 16 70(4) MeV (N_f = 2).
published_hypotheses: Definition: sigma_q = m_q <N|qbar q|N> = m_q dM_N/dm_q, a first derivative (Feynman-Hellmann) at the physical point, the lattice scale / QCD coupling held fixed (Eqs.(431)-(433),(446)).

Isospin-symmetric limit defined with the NEUTRAL pion mass (~135 MeV), per the sibling audit's read; the phenomenological Roy-Steiner value 59.1(3.5) MeV (1506.04142) is in the charged-pion convention, and the conversion shifts sigma_piN by 3.1(5) MeV (restated in 2609.05989 p.2).
Averages are over lattice results passing FLAG quality criteria (continuum, chiral, finite-volume, renormalization, excited-state ratings); N_f = 2+1 average error inflated ~10% for chi^2/dof = 1.23.
sigma_s(2+1+1) is a single-study value: MILC 12C's <N|ss|N> multiplied by the FLAG m_s average (Ref. [107]).
Excited-state (N pi, N pi pi) control 'remains an issue' (p.273) and 'the averages may change' (p.274): the 2.7-sigma N_f split is not attributed to sea charm.
'Shift in M_N due to nonzero quark masses' is the first-order (linear) reading of sigma; the review does not claim it equals the finite difference M_N - M_N(m_q = 0).
hypothesis_drift: RETAINED, named: the first-order (Feynman-Hellmann) character of sigma. massform.py:326-330 ('AT FIRST ORDER (H-LINEAR: the response at the physical point, with the QCD scale held fixed) ... it is not the finite share the field gives, which is OPEN'), massform.py:1789-1793 (sigma_fraction docstring 'the Feynman-Hellmann quark-mass part'), massform.py:1905-1912 (C2 'AT FIRST ORDER (H-LINEAR)'; FINITE_HIGGS_SHARE_EXCEEDS_HALF = None). Check F of the re-derivation shows this is load-bearing and not cosmetic: for M = M0 + c1 m + c32 m^(3/2), sigma - (M - M0) = c32 m^(3/2)/2 exactly, so FLAG's 'shift in M_N' sentence (quoted at massform.py:325-326, 1346-1349) is itself exact only at linear order. The tree does not flatten it.

ADDED by the tree, named as its own inference: 'i.e. with the Higgs' (massform.py:327-329). Under a real change of v the heavy-quark thresholds move Lambda_3; the tree keeps that part out of the READ rows and labels it CONTESTED (massform.py:352-363, 1860-1868). rederivation.outcome: ALL CHECKS PASS (exit 0; output in rederive/2411.04268.out). A0: m_N = 938.9187555 MeV exactly from the capture. A1/A2: f_l = 10.852909 % and 9.276628 % (exact over Fraction) -> 10.85 % / 9.28 % as the tree prints. B: (60.9-42.2)/sqrt(6.5^2+2.4^2) = 2.699 sigma = FLAG's 2.7 (uncorrelated). sigma_s averages agree to 0.36 sigma; the two f_l differ by 1.15 sigma. D0: massform.F_LIGHT equals A. D1: the READ-row maximum (0.1719) is Ji's row, not FLAG. D2/D3: sigma_piN + sigma_s must reach 466.0 MeV for the payload share to reach 1/2; every value in play (both FLAG centrals, +3 and +5 sigma linear, phenomenology +5 sigma with sigma_s +5 sigma = 153.5 MeV, two-loop BChPT 100.8 MeV, even + sigma_c 107 = 208.9 MeV) stays below (max 0.2243), and the tree's own largest_central_reading() with the moved datum substituted stays 0.1719 < 1/2. E: the 3.1 MeV isospin shift is 0.33 pp of f_l. F (sympy, exact): for M = M0 + c1 m + c32 m^(3/2), sigma - (M - M0) = c32 m^(3/2)/2, and sigma/shift = p for a pure power m^p -- so sigma equals the finite 'shift in M_N' only at linear order, which is exactly why H-LINEAR is a named hypothesis. G (INFO, not a finding): Hoferichter 59.1(3.5) or 59.0(3.5) against 42.2(2.4) is 3.96-3.98 sigma uncorrelated; 56.0 in the neutral convention gives 3.25 sigma, consistent with FLAG's 'around three standard deviations' -- which value/convention FLAG used for Hoferichter 23 is NOT read here. (The sibling qcd-trace audit's paraphrase of 2506.23902, '42.2 vs 59.0 MeV, 3.2 sigma', does not reproduce as uncorrelated arithmetic with a 3.5 MeV error; recorded as a discrepancy of transcription or convention, not an error of any paper.)

lacked_data: M's hypothesis tested for this result. What FLAG had (literature to its 2024 closing): lattice sigma_piN at N_f = 2+1 and 2+1+1 with excited-state treatments that could not yet separate N-pi / N-pi-pi / N-sigma states, and one-loop chiral fits. What came later: variational N-sigma bases (2412.13138, 2609.05989; not yet at the physical point) and a two-loop BChPT re-analysis of the same N_f = 2+1 lattice data giving 55.9(2.5) MeV (2508.11435, restated). EVIDENCE FOR M's thesis on the NUMBER: the N_f = 2+1 average 42.2(2.4) is plausibly low for want of exactly that data/method, and FLAG itself says 'the averages may change'. EVIDENCE AGAINST it mattering here: the tree never chose the 2+1 value (it prints both and names the tension), the conclusion that uses these numbers -- C2, 'at first order a change of phi moves most of atomic mass' = False -- needs sigma_piN + sigma_s = 466 MeV and every value in play, to 5 sigma, is at most 178 MeV (208.9 MeV even adding contested charm); and the READ-row maximum is set by Ji's row, not by FLAG. The interpretation (sigma as first-order response) is a theorem-level definition (Feynman-Hellmann), not data, and the tree already refuses to read it as the finite share (OPEN). So the authors did lack data that bears on the 2+1 central value, and having it would move that value by up to ~14 MeV, but it does not change the conclusion the tree draws.
grade_evidence: (1) Statement as used: every numeral and quoted sentence at massform.py:320-338 / 1314-1350 matches the at-source read of 2411.04268 recorded by the sibling DOCKET 67 audit (sigma-term-scan.json, pp.260-275). (2) Hypotheses: the first-order (Feynman-Hellmann) character is retained and named (H-LINEAR), and the tree refuses to read sigma as the finite share (FINITE_HIGGS_SHARE_EXCEEDS_HALF = None); the only unnamed items are a 3.1 MeV isospin-convention label (0.33 pp of f_l) and the single-study origin of sigma_s(2+1+1), neither of which moves anything -- recorded as discrepancies, not errors. (3) Re-derivation agrees: f_l 10.85 % / 9.28 % exact; 2.7 sigma reproduces (2.699); sympy check F confirms that equating sigma with a shift is exact only at linear order, which is what H-LINEAR says. (4) Data: the contested datum (sigma_piN at N_f = 2+1, 42.2 vs ~56-59) moves f_l by <= 1.5 pp, while C2 needs a light sigma sum of 466 MeV; the tree's own verdict function, with the datum substituted at +5 sigma, returns 0.1719 < 1/2. Not NARROWED (no hypothesis the tree's use needs is dropped; the conventions left unnamed do not restrict the class on which the use holds). Not DATA-DEPENDENT (the moved/contested datum does not move the conclusion). Not WRONG (no counterexample or contradiction found). CAVEAT on the read: this stage could not open the PDF itself (alphaXiv quota exhausted; arxiv.org egress-blocked); the grade rests on the sibling audit's at-source transcription corroborated by the tree's independent transcription.
what_would_change_the_grade: A direct read of 2411.04268v3 Sec.10.4.4 showing any numeral or quoted sentence at massform.py:1314-1350 differs from the source (-> discrepancy recorded; grade re-examined). A physical-point lattice or phenomenological sigma_piN + sigma_s approaching ~466 MeV (none exists or is expected; current values 87-104 MeV) would make C2 DATA-DEPENDENT. A use of sigma as the FINITE Higgs share (dropping H-LINEAR) would make it NARROWED (check F). A later FLAG edition replacing Eqs.(447)-(450) would change data_at_publication but, on the computed margin, not the conclusion.
